Overview

Amman as a Business Centre

Amman is the political and commercial centre of Jordan. According to the Department of Statistics, the Amman area held about 4.64 million people at the end of 2021, roughly 42 percent of the Kingdom's population. Ministries, the central bank, the Amman Stock Exchange and the head offices of most Jordanian banks, insurers and listed companies are concentrated in the city. The Amman Chamber of Commerce, founded by forty merchants in 1923, reports that its roughly 42,000 member establishments provide around 567,000 jobs. Trading houses, family business groups, construction and real estate developers, pharmaceutical manufacturers, technology firms and the regional offices of international organisations and aid agencies all operate from Amman, which also serves as a base for business in Iraq, Syria and the wider Levant.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Amman because so much of Jordan's corporate, financial and public decision-making sits there. Investors and lenders need to understand family-controlled groups whose holdings span trading, real estate and services. Contractors and donors working on publicly funded and internationally financed projects need procurement integrity checks. Regional companies use Amman entities to manage operations in neighbouring markets, which raises questions about ultimate ownership, sanctions exposure and the movement of funds. Litigants and arbitral parties need asset, witness and corporate history research for proceedings before the Amman courts or in arbitration. Most of the relevant records and much of the reporting are in Arabic, which shapes how research is planned.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Amman

01

Family business group diligence

Many Amman companies belong to family groups with interests across trading, real estate, banking and services. Before investment, acquisition or joint venture, we map group structures, related parties, principals' other business interests and litigation history, so that clients understand who controls the counterparty and where conflicts may lie.

02

Procurement and donor-funded project integrity

Ministries, utilities and international donors headquartered or represented in Amman award significant contracts. We research bidders, subcontractors and agents for ownership links, prior disputes, adverse media and connections to public officials, helping compliance teams identify conflicts of interest and integrity concerns before award or disbursement.

03

Regional trade and sanctions exposure

Amman entities are often used to trade with or manage operations in Iraq and Syria. We review counterparties, intermediaries and shipping or payment patterns for links to restricted parties and for unclear ownership, supporting clients' own sanctions and export-control compliance decisions.

04

Asset research for Amman proceedings

Creditors and claimants with judgments or awards against Jordanian parties need to know what can be reached. We research company holdings, real estate interests disclosed in public sources, related entities and transfers, giving counsel a sourced picture before enforcement steps in the Amman courts.

05

Executive and partner background checks

Banks, investors and multinationals appointing senior executives, agents or distributors in Amman commission background research. We verify career history, directorships and reputation through lawful sources and Arabic-language media, with any collection of personal data planned around Jordan's Personal Data Protection Law.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Amman

Amman courts and commercial section

The Amman Court of First Instance is the principal first-instance court for the capital, and the Court of Cassation, Jordan's highest ordinary court, also sits in Amman. The Court of First Instance has opened a section dedicated exclusively to commercial cases and disputes, staffed by its own judges, following recommendations of the Royal Committee for Developing the Judiciary and Enhancing the Rule of Law. Proceedings are in Arabic, so documents and investigative reports intended for the court usually need certified Arabic translation.

Arbitration and the new centre

Arbitration is widely used in Jordanian commercial and construction contracts. As of August 2026, amendments to the Arbitration Law provide for a statutory Jordan Arbitration Centre, a private non-profit body governed by a board appointed by the Council of Ministers, with rules covering emergency arbitrators, expedited procedure, consolidation and disclosure of third-party funding. Reporting indicates the centre had not yet opened, so parties should confirm its status with counsel before relying on it.

Chamber of commerce and company records

The Amman Chamber of Commerce, established in 1923, is Jordan's first officially established chamber and represents commercial, service and agricultural businesses in the capital. Membership and certificate records issued through the chamber complement the national company records held by the Companies Control Department, described on the Jordan page. Matching chamber, registry and court information is usually needed to establish who operates a given Amman business.

Capital-city regulators

Jordan's main economic regulators and enforcement bodies are based in Amman, including the Central Bank of Jordan, the Jordan Securities Commission, the Amman Stock Exchange and the Integrity and Anti-Corruption Commission. Their published decisions, disclosures by listed companies and enforcement announcements are useful sources when researching Amman-based banks, issuers and their directors, and are reviewed in Arabic and English where available.

Growth and municipal development

Amman has expanded rapidly over recent decades, absorbing large inflows of residents, including refugees from regional conflicts, and the Greater Amman Municipality has run successive infrastructure and planning programmes to keep pace. Fast growth has brought large real estate, transport and utility projects, which in turn create exposure to contractor failure, land and development disputes and procurement irregularities that investigative research can help clients identify early.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Amman

TDSC has no office in Amman and handles Amman matters from Nashville. We start by confirming with the client and its Jordanian counsel the purpose of the work, whether an investment, a procurement review, a judgment enforcement, arbitration support or an internal inquiry, because Jordan's Personal Data Protection Law requires a documented lawful basis. Research draws on company and chamber records, court material available to counsel, Amman Stock Exchange disclosures, regulatory announcements and Arabic and English media. Where on-the-ground enquiries are needed, we coordinate qualified local professionals and agree methods with counsel in advance. Every matter is screened for sanctions exposure, which is often relevant given Amman's links to neighbouring markets.

Questions

Amman: Frequently Asked Questions

Can TDSC research a family-owned group based in Amman?

Yes. We map the group's companies, shareholders and directors using available registry and chamber records, review litigation and regulatory history, and analyse Arabic and English media. Family groups often hold interests through several entities, so the work focuses on identifying related parties and controlling individuals. Findings are sourced so clients and counsel can assess them.

Which court hears commercial disputes in Amman?

Commercial claims at first instance are generally heard by the Amman Court of First Instance, which has a section dedicated exclusively to commercial cases. Appeals go to the Court of Appeal and then the Court of Cassation, which sits in Amman. Many commercial contracts instead provide for arbitration. Counsel determines the forum, and we shape research to it.

Is there an arbitration centre in Amman?

Amendments to Jordan's Arbitration Law reported in 2026 provide for a statutory Jordan Arbitration Centre with modern rules, including emergency arbitrators and third-party funding disclosure. Reporting from August 2026 indicates it had not yet opened. Parties should confirm its status and the applicable rules with Jordanian counsel before drafting clauses or filing.

Can you check whether an Amman counterparty trades with sanctioned parties?

We can research the counterparty's ownership, management, affiliates and trading links, including activity in Iraq and Syria, and screen identified parties against public sanctions lists. The results support, but do not replace, the client's own compliance determination. TDSC, as a US company, does not accept work that would breach applicable sanctions.

Do research reports for Amman matters need to be in Arabic?

Reports for the client are normally prepared in English. Where findings or source documents will be filed with a Jordanian court or used in local proceedings, counsel will usually need certified Arabic translations. We identify Arabic sources in reports and can coordinate translation through providers counsel approves.
